name: FP Series Submersible Pump
summary: Slim internal pumps supplied with a perforated spray bar, so they can filter, circulate or feed a fountain. Four sizes from 300 to 1,350 L/h, with permanent-magnet motors and stainless shafts.
bestFor: Adding gentle, spread-out circulation to a medium tank or powering a simple internal filter.
highlights: Spray bar included for even flow along the tank
watchOut: Spray bars sit high by design, so expect surface movement and some CO2 loss.

name: HL Crossflow Wave Pump
summary: A tube-shaped crossflow pump that pushes a wide sheet of water along the tank, a bit like a gyre, and can also aerate. It uses a DC variable-speed drive with a digital display. Sizes run from a 20 cm unit to a 70 cm bar for very large aquariums.
bestFor: Long tanks where you want even flow across the whole front-to-back depth.
highlights: DC variable speed with LED display
Can aerate as well as circulate
watchOut: Boyu does not publish flow figures, and the two big models draw 100 to 200 W.

name: PGB Series Submersible Pump
summary: Tall, narrow submersible pumps with a long intake tube, built to sit upright in a corner or on an undergravel uplift. Three sizes from 740 to 1,565 L/h with up to 2.4 m of head.
bestFor: Undergravel plates, sump returns or DIY top filters that need decent head in a narrow space.

name: SP-100 / SP-101 Series Powerhead
summary: A long-running range of small submersible powerheads with a venturi tube, a flow adjuster and an optional spray nozzle. Nine sizes run from a tiny 300 L/h unit to 1,850 L/h. Useful as a return pump, for driving an undergravel plate or just adding surface movement.
bestFor: Anyone needing a cheap general-purpose pump for circulation, a DIY filter or a small sump return.
highlights: Venturi air injection and adjustable flow
watchOut: The venturi and spray bar add a lot of surface agitation, which is not what you want on a CO2-injected tank.

name: SP-1000 Series Submersible Pump
summary: Compact multi-purpose submersible pumps that can push water, drive a fountain outlet or power a small filter. Five sizes from 300 to 1,400 L/h, with stainless steel shafts and resin-potted motors.
bestFor: Small sump returns, DIY filters and general water moving jobs around the fish room.
highlights: Up to 2 m head on the largest
Works as pump, fountain or filter pump
watchOut: Power use is on the high side for the flow on the bigger models (34 W for 1,400 L/h).

name: WM Series Wavemaker
summary: Round-bodied flow pumps that throw a broad, turbulent stream rather than a narrow jet, on a swivelling mount. The range covers single pumps (WM-101, WM-1, WM-2, WM-15), a DC 12 to 24 V WM-25 on a suction mount, and multi-pump kits with a wave controller (WM-3 and WM-4).
bestFor: Medium and large planted tanks with dead spots behind hardscape, where you want circulation without a blasting jet.
highlights: Swivel mount points the flow any direction
WM-3 and WM-4 kits add a wave timer controller
WM-25 runs on DC 12 to 24 V, 5,500 L/h

specs.Mounting: Suction cup / rim bracket, adjustable angle

watchOut: Boyu only gives flow for the WM-25; the others are rated by tank size, and the marketing leans towards marine use.

name: WM-50 / WM-102 DC Wavemaker
summary: DC-driven wavemakers with an external digital controller that stores custom wave and flow programmes. WM-102 is a twin-pump set; WM-50 is a single, much stronger pump. Both run on a safe 24 V supply.
bestFor: Large tanks where you want adjustable, pulsed circulation from a controller.
watchOut: These are very strong pumps; most planted tanks will run them well below maximum.

name: AA Series Submersible Pump
summary: Grey and blue submersible pumps with a carry handle on the bigger sizes, running from 300 to 4300 L/h. Sold as "power liquid filter" pumps, they are general-purpose water movers.
bestFor: A sump return or water-transfer pump where you need decent head height for the money.
highlights: Up to 4 m head on the AA9000
watchOut: Power draw is high on the big models (116 to 125 W for AA6000 and AA9000); an efficient DC pump costs more upfront but less to run.

name: ECO DC Variable Pump
summary: A 24 V DC pump with a digital remote that gives 20 steps of steady flow, two wave modes and a feed pause. It also cuts out and alarms if it runs dry.
bestFor: A sump return on a large tank where turning the flow down precisely matters more than raw price.
highlights: 20-step flow control plus fast and slow wave modes

specs.Motor: 24 V DC, accepts 100 to 240 V AC input

watchOut: Even at its lowest setting it is a big pump, sized for large systems rather than a normal planted tank.

name: P Series Submersible Pump
summary: A long-running range of grey and black submersible pumps from 320 to 3000 L/h with a blue flow dial on the smaller models.
bestFor: Driving a DIY filter, a sump return or a water-change setup on a budget.
highlights: Flow adjustment dial on small and mid sizes
watchOut: The large models draw 66 to 88 W, which is a lot for a pump running around the clock.

name: P-608 / P-908 Power Head
summary: A classic square aquarium powerhead, the same pump used on Dophin top filters. Fitted with its sponge it doubles as a basic internal filter.
bestFor: Driving a top filter or giving an old-school tank extra flow.
highlights: Can run a top filter or undergravel setup
Sponge attachment shown on the box
watchOut: At 16 to 29 W these are thirsty next to modern DC circulation pumps.

name: PC Series Submersible Pump
summary: Compact square submersible pumps from 300 to 5000 L/h. The three largest get a carry handle and a flow controller.
bestFor: A return pump for a sump, a DIY filter or water changes, sized to your head height.
highlights: Up to 3 m head on the largest
Flow controller on PC-3000, PC-4000, PC-5000
watchOut: Watts climb steeply on the bigger models (120 W for the PC-5000), so check running cost if it will run all day.

name: PH Series Submersible Pump
summary: Small black submersible pumps from 300 to 1250 L/h, the sort used to drive a small DIY filter, a spray bar or water changes.
bestFor: Driving a DIY sponge or box filter, adding a little extra flow, or topping up from a bucket.
watchOut: Head figures are the maximum lift with zero flow, so size up if you need to push water more than a metre.

name: WP Wave Pump
summary: A compact circulation pump on a suction-cup mount that tilts 100 degrees and swivels 360. Two sizes, rated 2000 and 5000 L/h.
bestFor: Adding gentle circulation to a larger planted tank to move CO2 and nutrients into dead spots.

specs.Mount: Suction cup, 100 degree tilt, 360 degree rotation

watchOut: It gives steady flow only, no wave controller, and the WP-3000 can be too strong for tanks under about 200 litres.

name: compactON
summary: compactON is a family of small, quiet water pumps for moving water around a tank, a sump or a DIY filter. The smaller ones stick to the glass with suckers, and most sizes have a flow dial.
bestFor: Return pumps for sumps, DIY filters or water features in a planted setup.
highlights: Adjustable flow on all but the 5000
2100 and up can run outside the water as well
watchOut: Output drops quickly with head height, so check the pump curve if you are lifting water a long way.

name: streamON+
summary: streamON+ is a compact propeller pump on a magnetic mount, used to push water around the tank rather than through a filter. It swivels on a ball joint and has a slider to throttle the outflow, and it is very frugal with power.
bestFor: High-tech planted tanks that need extra circulation to push CO2 and nutrients into dense stem groups.
highlights: Magnet mount, easy to move and angle
watchOut: Even the smallest moves a lot of water, so on a nano or with delicate fish, start on the lowest setting and aim it at the glass.

name: Universal
summary: The Universal pumps are the long-running workhorses of the Eheim range, used in sumps, trickle filters and fish houses. They can sit in the water or outside it, and a built-in prefilter protects the impeller.
bestFor: Sump returns or external plumbing on larger planted systems where you want a very durable pump.
highlights: Run submerged or inline outside the tank
watchOut: The bigger sizes draw 65 to 80 W, far more than a modern DC pump of similar output.

name: OptiMax
summary: A range of adjustable water pumps from 300 to 5,000 L/h, for circulation, running a DIY filter or returning water from a sump. The smaller models are submersible only, while the 800 and up can also run dry outside the tank. Flow is adjustable on every model.
bestFor: Sump returns, DIY filters, water changes or extra circulation in a larger planted tank.
highlights: 800 and larger can be installed dry (inline) or submerged
watchOut: The 2000 and up draw 30 to 80 W, which adds up on your bill and adds heat to the water if submerged.

name: CDP DC Frequency Pump
summary: A 24 V DC pump with an external controller, from 3,500 to 10,000 L/h. SunSun also sells the same pump as SDP and ZDP.
bestFor: Sump returns on mid to large tanks.

name: CHJ Multi-Function Pump
summary: A broad range of AC pumps from 500 to 6,000 L/h. The CHJ-02 versions come with a filter column.
bestFor: Sump returns and powering filters on tanks of most sizes.

name: CTB Frequency Pump
summary: An efficient pump range from 2,500 to 7,000 L/h, suited to sumps and filter feeds. Six sizes.
bestFor: Mid to large sump returns.

name: CTP Frequency Pump
summary: A frequency pump range from 3,000 to 16,000 L/h, with low wattage for its flow. Twelve sizes.
bestFor: Sump returns on large tanks.

name: CW Wavemaker
summary: A 24 V propeller wavemaker with an external controller, from 4,000 to 20,000 L/h. Standard models are adjustable across a wide range; S models run at a fixed rate.
bestFor: Planted tanks from 50 cm up that need gentle, adjustable circulation.

name: HJ Mini Submersible Pump
summary: Tiny pumps from 200 to 800 L/h, used in desktop tanks, small fountains and DIY nano filters. The smallest are under 4 cm across.
bestFor: Nano tanks, all-in-one rear chambers and small DIY projects.

name: HJ Series Submersible Pump
summary: SunSun's HJ-500 to HJ-6000 pumps, a common choice as sump return pumps in its own cabinet tanks. Ten sizes from 500 to 6,800 L/h.
bestFor: Sump returns and closed-loop circulation on mid to large tanks.
watchOut: The large models are power hungry (150 W for the HJ-6000); a DC or frequency pump will cost less to run.

name: HJ-41 Series Submersible Pump
summary: A long-running line of compact AC submersible pumps from 400 to 3,000 L/h, with a round intake cover. Useful for powering a DIY filter, a return from a small sump or a water-change setup.
bestFor: Small sumps, DIY filters and general water moving.
watchOut: Older AC design, so power use is high for the flow on the bigger models; DC pumps are quieter and adjustable.

name: HQJ and CQJ Submersible Pump
summary: Small pumps from 350 to 1,600 L/h in several body styles, including 12 V DC versions (HQJ-D). The HQJ-500G and 700G are fitted to many SunSun tanks.
bestFor: Desktop and small tank filtration, rear chambers and top filters.

name: JDP DC Frequency Pump
summary: SunSun's popular 24 V DC return pump with a controller that steps flow through five levels on the bigger models. Seven sizes from 1,000 to 18,000 L/h; Q versions add a one-touch feed pause.
bestFor: Sump returns and closed loops where you want adjustable, quiet flow.

name: JGP Low Water Level Pump
summary: A bottom-intake pump with dry-run protection and a ceramic shaft, able to pump down to about 5 mm. Six sizes from 1,000 to 4,500 L/h.
bestFor: Water changes and draining tanks, shallow sumps.
watchOut: High wattage for the flow (130 W on the largest), so better for occasional jobs than 24/7 use.

name: JHP DC Pump
summary: A vertical 24 V DC pump from 2,000 to 6,000 L/h, with a slim cylindrical body. It fits tight sump sections.
bestFor: Sump returns where space is tight.

name: JP-06 Series Submersible Pump
summary: Multi-purpose AC pumps from 450 to 3,800 L/h with a boxy body and wide outlet sizes. Eight sizes.
bestFor: Sump returns and powering external filters on mid-size tanks.
watchOut: Power draw is high on the large models compared with SunSun's frequency pumps.

name: JP-G Series Submersible Pump
summary: Compact pumps from the 250 L/h JP-230G used in many SunSun desktop tanks, up to 1,800 L/h. The GS versions are rated a little differently from the G pump of the same size, so compare flow and head model by model.
bestFor: Nano tank filters, small sumps and DIY builds.

name: JP-GL Low Water Level Pump
summary: A pump that can draw water down to about 5 mm, with a ceramic shaft and a 360 degree intake. Five sizes from 600 to 1,600 L/h.
bestFor: Shallow sumps and emptying tanks during water changes.
highlights: Pumps down to about 5 mm of water

name: JQP Submersible Pump and Filter
summary: An efficient compact pump range from 500 to 3,500 L/h, sold bare or with a filter column (JQP-F). Up to 3.6 m head.
bestFor: Sump returns and filter feeds on small to mid tanks.

specs.F models: The F models add a filter sponge on the intake so the pump works as a simple internal filter

name: JTP Frequency Pump
summary: Efficient frequency-controlled pumps from 1,800 to 5,800 L/h (including 12/24 V DC models) plus the smaller JTP-2000 to 3000. They move a lot of water for their wattage.
bestFor: Sump returns where running cost matters.

name: JTP-R Frequency Pump
summary: The larger JTP range, from 4,000 to 16,000 L/h, for big sumps and closed loops. Wattage stays reasonable for the flow.
bestFor: Large display tanks with a sump.
watchOut: Far too much flow for most planted tanks unless you are running a big sump.

name: JVP Wavemaker
summary: SunSun's classic magnet-mount wavemakers, from a tiny 2,000 L/h unit to the 24,000 L/h twin-head JVP-402. The head can be aimed, and several models rotate on the magnet.
bestFor: Adding circulation to large planted tanks so CO2 and nutrients reach every plant.
watchOut: Pick a small one for a planted tank; too much flow flattens stems and blows substrate around.

name: STP Eco Pump
summary: An efficient pump that works submerged or dry-mounted, from 3,000 to 8,000 L/h. The STP-3800 drives the barrel filters in SunSun's H3TS and HYTX-IT tanks.
bestFor: Sump returns and driving external pressure filters.

name: XDP DC Frequency Pump
summary: A Xiaoli-line 24 V DC pump from 1,000 to 6,800 L/h. S versions push harder against head.
bestFor: Sump returns and filter feeds on small to large tanks.

name: XGP Low Water Level Pump
summary: A pump with a thermal cut-out against running dry, a 360 degree intake and the ability to pump down to about 5 mm. Six sizes from 500 to 3,500 L/h.
bestFor: Water changes and shallow sumps.

name: XQP Submersible Pump
summary: Compact Xiaoli-line pumps in 500, 1,000 and 1,500 L/h, also sold with a filter box as XQP-F. Low wattage for the flow.
bestFor: Small sumps, rear-chamber tanks and DIY filters.

name: XVA Wave Pump
summary: A submersible wave pump for glass up to 12 mm, from 6,000 to 10,000 L/h, with a ceramic shaft and a head that turns through 180 degrees. Each size also comes as an E version.
bestFor: Circulation in tanks up to about a metre.

name: XVP Wavemaker
summary: A Xiaoli-line magnet-mount wavemaker in three sizes from 2,500 to 12,000 L/h.
bestFor: Circulation in mid to large tanks.

name: ZHL Low Water Level Pump
summary: A carry-handle pump with a 360 degree bottom intake and dry-run protection, from 1,000 to 4,500 L/h. SunSun also sells it as the CHL series.
bestFor: Water changes, tank moves and draining.
watchOut: Built for moving water rather than running quietly all day.

name: ZSP Frequency Pump
summary: A Zhizhen-line frequency pump from 2,500 to 14,000 L/h. Ten sizes, up to 7 m head.
bestFor: Sump returns on mid to large tanks.

name: ZZP Cross-Flow Wave Pump
summary: A long, gyre-style cross-flow pump (29 cm) that produces a wide sheet of flow, with a separate 24 V controller. One size for 70 to 120 cm tanks.
bestFor: Larger planted tanks where you want broad, even flow instead of a jet.

name: Sigma Water Pump
summary: Small submersible DC pumps with an adjustable flow dial. They are the return pumps UNS pairs with its all-in-one tanks, and they also work as a general-purpose pump in a sump or DIY build.
bestFor: Powering the rear chamber of an all-in-one tank, or a small custom filter or sump.
highlights: Four sizes from about 300 L/h to 1,500 L/h
Flow is adjustable on the pump
Low-voltage DC (5 V on the Sigma 5, 12 V on the others)
watchOut: Pick the size to match your tank's chamber; the listed flow drops quickly as head height goes up.
